title: Open Values Asks/Offers Index v0.1
description: A ready-to-show version of the asks and offers file, with each related category, guide and organisation looked up and filled in, plus counts and filter lists. pipeline/build_initiatives.js builds it from content/asks-offers.json into app/data/asks-offers-index.json; change the source file, not this one.

format.description: Always "open-values-asks-offers-index". Tells a reader which Open Values format this is.

version.description: The version of the index format this file follows. Must start with 0.1.0.

standard.description: Always "open-values-standard", the standard this format belongs to.

built.description: The date of the asks and offers file this index was built from, copied from that file's updated field, as YYYY-MM-DD.

purpose.description: A sentence saying what this index is for.

generatedFrom.description: The asks and offers file this index was built from, its date, and its hash, so anyone can check the index against it.

publication.description: Copied unchanged from the asks and offers file: how it is published and what must stay out of it.

counts.description: Totals across the file: items, asks, offers, templates, live items, and how many different categories, guides, initiatives, values and regions they mention.

sections.description: The two groups a board shows, asks and offers, with how many items are in each.

filters.description: The distinct values an app can offer as filters, each list sorted alphabetically.

principles.description: Copied unchanged from the asks and offers file: the rules it follows, one short sentence each.

items.description: Every ask and offer in the file, in file order, with its related categories, guides and initiatives looked up and filled in.

note.description: One sentence saying what the source shows.

source.description: The web address of the source, starting with http:// or https://.

asof.description: The year the source was checked, as four digits, such as "2026".

path.description: Always "content/asks-offers.json", the file this index is built from.

updated.description: The asks and offers file's own updated date, as YYYY-MM-DD.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 hash of the asks and offers file text at build time, in 64 lowercase hex characters.

status.description: Whether the file is a format seed (templates only), active (real asks and offers are being published), or archived.

storage.description: How the records are stored, such as "single-json-file".

relay.description: The ways the file may be passed around, such as a static host or a repository discussion. A relay only moves the file and has no say over it.

identity.description: How the people behind asks and offers are identified, such as pseudonymous or named by choice.

liveDatabase.description: Always false: asks and offers live in a file, not in a live database.

privacy.description: What must never be published in the file, such as private contact details, exact addresses or the names of people being helped.

items.description: How many asks and offers the file holds in all.

templates.description: How many items have status template.

live.description: How many items have status live. The schema fixes this at 0 while the file is a seed.

categories.description: How many different categories the items point at.

guides.description: How many different guides the items point at.

initiatives.description: How many different initiatives the items point at.

values.description: How many different values the items name.

regions.description: How many different regions the items name.

label.description: The heading to show for the section, such as "Asks".

kind.description: The item kind the section holds: "ask" or "offer".

count.description: How many items are in the section.

values.description: Every value named by at least one item.

regions.description: Every region named by at least one item.

categories.description: Every category id named by at least one item.

guides.description: Every guide slug named by at least one item.

initiatives.description: Every initiative code named by at least one item.

label.description: The category name shown to readers, such as "Password managers". If the id is not found in the category index, this repeats the id.

type.description: What kind of thing the category covers: Products, Services, Media, Organizations, or Initiatives.

domain.description: The broad area the category belongs to in the site navigation, such as "Tech & digital".

group.description: The group within that area, such as "Digital services", when the category has one.

file.description: The name of the category dataset file in app/data/, such as "digital-services.json".

n.description: How many entries the category dataset holds.

title.description: The guide's title, taken from its title line or first heading.

path.description: Where the guide lives in the repository, such as "content/guides/private-messaging.md".

hash.description: The link fragment that opens the guide in the app, such as "#guide/private-messaging".

code.description: The initiative code, such as "eff", as used in the initiatives dataset.

name.description: The name of the organization or project, such as "Electronic Frontier Foundation". If the code is not found in the dataset, this repeats the code.

brand.description: A short tag for what the initiative works on, such as "digital rights".

focuses.description: The topics the initiative is filed under, such as "Privacy" or "Open source".

description.description: One sentence on what the initiative does.

legitimacy.description: A line saying who the initiative is, with the source that backs it.

actPath.description: How a reader can act on the initiative: a link to follow, or a plain instruction.

scoreSignals.description: Three of the initiative's scores from the initiatives dataset, each from 0 to 100: impact, transparency, and ways_to_help.

links.description: Links for the initiative, each with a label and a url, copied from the initiatives dataset.

categories.description: The related categories, each with its id, label and where it sits in the site.

guides.description: The related guides, each with its title, file path and app link.

initiatives.description: The related initiatives, each with its name, description, source and how to act on it.

label.description: The item kind as a heading: "Ask" or "Offer".

listLabel.description: The heading for the list below it: "Needs" for an ask, "Offers" for an offer.

items.description: The item's needs list for an ask, or its offers list for an offer.

line.description: One sentence saying who the initiative is and what it does.

source.description: The source that backs that sentence.

kind.description: Whether the way to act is a link ("url") or a written instruction ("plain").

label.description: The text to show for the action, such as "Website".

url.description: The web address to follow. Required when kind is url.

instruction.description: What the reader should do, in words. Required when kind is plain.

id.description: A unique name for this ask or offer, in lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, such as "ask-digital-safety-clinic".

kind.description: Whether this is an ask (someone needs help) or an offer (someone can give help).

status.description: Where the item stands: template (an example to copy), seed, live (a real request or offer), or archived.

title.description: A short heading for the item, such as "We need help running a digital-safety clinic".

summary.description: One or two sentences saying who needs or offers what.

prompt.description: The question or offer as the person would put it to a reader, such as "Can you help run a calm digital-safety session for people who do not want jargon?"

audience.description: The kinds of people or groups the item is for, such as "library" or "mutual-aid group".

values.description: Which of the ten shared values the item serves, such as "autonomy" or "community". At least one.

regions.description: Where the item applies: US, UK, EU, or global. At least one.

action.description: The item's kind as a heading, and its list of needs or offers.

related.description: The categories, guides and initiatives the item points at, looked up and filled in.

receipts.description: Sources a reader can follow to check the claims or resources the item relies on. At least one.

limits.description: What the item must not be used for or must not publish, one sentence each, such as "Do not post invite links publicly." At least one.
